items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: Even though Blakey feathers the bass drum and all of those guys, and so do I.

ctx.x: Okay, even up and down eighth notes.

Right. And I like to play that kind of music because that freed me up, which a lot of guys didn’t. See a lot of guys, a lot of the swing players played four on the floor. Even though Blakey feathers the bass drum and all of those guys, and so do I. But it’s not like a pounding four on the floor. We call it four on the floor. But I like to — once I started hearing some guys dropping bombs, that’s when I said now that frees me up to like not be necessarily — because once the bass amps came in, the timekeeper in the…

player, really. You know. He’s the one that’s laying the time down. And I’m there to shade and color. Somebody’ll say, “well it’s dragging” or “it’s rushing.” I mean yeah, you can put an edge on the beat or put it behind the beat or whatever. I mean I’ve got a Miles’ Davis record, “Miles at the Black Hawk” when they start “Bye Bye Blackbird” at a certain tempo, and it’s almost a ballad by the time it ends. But it’s swinging all the way down.
